clue.text: A good way around European anxiety

indicators.note: the phrase for a long distance is wrapped about the abbreviation for European

parts.note: a good way off means far

explanation.surface: A traveller's worry about a long European trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear and anxiety are near synonyms for a state of dread or worry.

clue.text: Do note those voting against a game

parts.note: taken as written
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
the noes are those voting no in a division

explanation.surface: An instruction to record which people opposed a sporting motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb but just supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominoes is a game played with spotted tiles, so it is one example of a game.

clue.text: An element of air mixed with mud

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Something in the air when it is stirred with mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Radium is a radioactive chemical element discovered by the Curies.

clue.text: Polish off cod, say, outside home

indicators.note: outside tells us the creature word goes round the word for home

parts.note: cod is an example of a fish
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Finishing a plate of cod at someone's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with a capital is a nationality trap; it is the verb, and cod is just one example of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish off a task or a meal is to complete it entirely.

clue.text: Beginning to feel stiff and cold

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word means just its first letter

parts.note: stiff and rigid both mean unbending

explanation.surface: Someone starting to feel stiff and chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means very cold in temperature, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Part of the neck of northern primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Describing the neck of a monkey from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The nape is the back part of the neck, below the skull.

clue.text: Menacing senior nurse holding hip?

indicators.note: holding means the nurse's title contains the fashionable word

parts.note: in British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward
hip and in both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A threatening head nurse clutching a patient's hip joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip' is not the joint but trendy; the question mark flags the trick. In Britain a sister is a senior ward nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes something threatening or ominous, a synonym of menacing.

clue.text: Well-mannered girl broadcasting

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young society girl
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A polite young woman presenting on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcasting' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym of ON AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave and courteous, close to well-mannered.

clue.text: Threaten devil will take the hindmost

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
the hindmost part is the end

explanation.surface: A menacing allusion to the saying 'devil take the hindmost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impending threatens or looms, so impend means to threaten.

clue.text: Time showering, perhaps for exercises

parts.note: showering is one way of raining, hence the 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Taking a shower after a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Training sessions are physical drills, so training stands for exercises.

clue.text: Parrot sheltered by screech-owls

indicators.note: sheltered by means the word is tucked away inside the following letters

explanation.surface: A parrot hiding among screeching owls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheltered by' finds the letters running across scrECH-Owls.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mindlessly, which is to echo them.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about illicit whisky in child's toy

indicators.note: about means the exclamation goes around the liquor

parts.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise
hooch is illicitly made or smuggled liquor

explanation.surface: A shocked discovery of bootleg whisky hidden in a toy.
explanation.walkthrough: Coo is a dated British cry of surprise; 'about' wraps it round the liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Children call a train a choo-choo, the nursery word for a locomotive.

clue.text: Fair method by judge

parts.note: a mode is a way or method
to rate something is to judge it

explanation.surface: A just procedure approved by a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate and fair both mean middling, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Lyric poem Delius initially set in Old English

indicators.note: set in means the letter is placed inside the abbreviation
initially picks the first letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: The composer Delius setting an Anglo-Saxon poem to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives D, which 'set in' places inside OE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem addressed to a subject.

clue.text: Reminiscent of benefit going in payment for accommodation

indicators.note: going in means the welfare word is placed inside the housing payment

parts.note: rent is what you pay for accommodation
the dole is British state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Welfare money being spent on rent.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is the everyday British name for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent of means evocative of or suggestive of something, a synonym for reminiscent of.

clue.text: Take into account son cried when upset

indicators.note: upset signals the letters of the two words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Pay attention to a boy who wept when distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider something is to weigh it up or take it into account.

clue.text: Straight run

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an adjective for a straight route, the other a verb for managing or running.

clue.text: Score damaged lustre

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters of the word are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A shiny finish that has been spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests a gouge; it is a match outcome. 'damaged' rearranges LUSTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A score, such as 2-1, is the final outcome of a game.

clue.text: Very cloudy days leading to ship being created by Noah

indicators.note: leading to puts the abbreviation before the vessel

parts.note: Noah built the ark before the flood

explanation.surface: The overcast days before Noah's flood while the ark was built.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy cloud cover makes the sky gloomy and dark.

clue.text: Run from long-legged bird, finding bamboo

indicators.note: run from means the letter for run departs from the bird

parts.note: a crane is a tall wading bird with long legs
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Fleeing a heron-like bird and stumbling on a bamboo thicket.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo stems are called canes, as in garden canes.

clue.text: Losing weight, fights in the ring with son, keeping moving

indicators.note: losing means the abbreviation for weight is dropped

parts.note: to wrestle is to fight in a wrestling ring

explanation.surface: A wrestler slimming down while sparring with his son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' takes W from WRESTLES, leaving RESTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A restless person cannot stay still, always fidgeting or on the move.

clue.text: Family animals up for a bit of a walk

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: pets are animals kept by a family

explanation.surface: The family pets keen to go out for a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: A single pace is one small part of a walk.

clue.text: He wraps out a few words

indicators.note: out signals the letters are rearranged, as in being put out of order

parts.note: the setter's slip: the fodder should read 'He raps', so the printed W is surplus and is dropped

explanation.surface: A man rapping out a short utterance.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's slip: as printed the fodder has a W that the answer lacks; the clue should read 'He raps out', with 'out' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a small group of words forming a unit.

clue.text: What strains company taking on moon explorer

indicators.note: taking on means the firm abbreviation adds the spacecraft after it

parts.note: a lunar lander is a craft that explores the moon

explanation.surface: A firm hiring a moon-landing craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a kitchen bowl with holes used for draining or straining food.

clue.text: Harass spies beginning to turn

parts.note: moles are spies planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pestering spies who are starting to defect.
explanation.definitionFit: To molest someone is to pester or harass them.
